topic.name: BRCA1
topic.short_description: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer gene
topic.seo_title: BRCA1 Cancer Research - Latest Studies & Findings | Your Cancer Breakthroughs
topic.seo_description: Explore BRCA1 gene research and hereditary breast/ovarian cancer diagnosis. Latest peer-reviewed studies, biomarker insights, and treatment advances.
topic.seo_intro:
BRCA1 is a tumor suppressor gene that plays a critical role in DNA repair and cancer prevention. When inherited mutations occur in the BRCA1 gene, they significantly increase the risk of developing hereditary breast cancer, ovarian cancer, and other malignancies. Understanding BRCA1 has revolutionized cancer diagnostics and personalized treatment approaches, making it one of the most extensively studied biomarkers in modern oncology.

Researchers worldwide are actively investigating BRCA1 mutations to improve early detection, risk assessment, and targeted therapeutic strategies. This biomarker has become essential in cancer screening protocols, helping identify high-risk individuals who may benefit from enhanced surveillance, preventive measures, or specialized treatments such as PARP inhibitors. The ongoing research continues to reveal how BRCA1 deficiencies affect tumor development and response to various cancer therapies.

On this page, you'll find the latest peer-reviewed research articles examining BRCA1 genetics, diagnostic methodologies, clinical implications, and emerging treatment innovations. Whether you're a patient, caregiver, or healthcare professional seeking evidence-based information about BRCA1 and its role in cancer care, these resources represent the cutting-edge scientific discoveries advancing our understanding of hereditary cancer risk.

articles.hook: BRCA1/2 carriers' treatment decisions shift with additional genetic risk modifier testing
articles.summary: Study examines how women with BRCA1/2 breast cancer gene mutations respond to additional genetic risk testing and make health decisions.

articles.title: Co-Pathogenic Role of BRCA1 and OBSCN Deletions in Chinese Familial Breast Cancer: A Case Report.
articles.hook: BRCA1 and OBSCN gene deletions together drive familial breast cancer
articles.summary: Two genetic mutations in BRCA1 and OBSCN genes together caused breast cancer in a Chinese family, a previously unreported combination.

articles.title: Regulation of antiviral and antitumor immunity by the BRCA1 pseudogene in human cancers.
articles.hook: BRCA1P1 pseudogene blocking activates antitumor immunity in breast cancer
articles.summary: Blocking a cancer-promoting RNA called BRCA1P1 triggers immune defenses that kill breast cancer and other tumors.

articles.title: Co-occurring rare germline DNA repair gene variants in BRCA1/BRCA2 implicated hereditary breast cancer families.
articles.hook: Rare DNA repair gene variants complicate hereditary breast cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Researchers found that hereditary breast cancer families carry multiple rare harmful DNA repair gene variants beyond BRCA1/BRCA2, complicating genetic test interpretation.

articles.title: JPI-547, a novel dual inhibitor of PARP1/2 and tankyrase is more effective than first-generation PARP inhibitors in preclinical BRCA1/2-mutated cancer models.
articles.hook: JPI-547 dual PARP/tankyrase inhibitor outperforms first-generation PARP inhibitors in BRCA1/2-mutated cancers
articles.summary: JPI-547, a new drug targeting PARP and tankyrase, outperforms existing treatments in BRCA1/2-mutated cancers, including resistant cases.

articles.title: Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer: Overview of Gene-Specific Risks and Challenges in Genetics Care Delivery.
articles.hook: BRCA1/2 genetic testing identifies hereditary breast and ovarian cancer risk
articles.summary: Genetic testing for BRCA1/2 and related genes identifies breast and ovarian cancer risk, enabling preventive surgery and surveillance to reduce cancer incidence.

articles.title: Whole exome sequencing reveals rare DNA repair gene variants in BRCA1/2-negative Arab early-onset breast cancer patients.
articles.hook: Rare DNA repair variants explain BRCA1/2-negative early-onset breast cancer in Arabs
articles.summary: Researchers identified rare DNA repair gene variants in Arab women with early-onset breast cancer who lack BRCA1/2 mutations.

articles.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals immune microenvironment heterogeneity in BRCA1-mutated and sporadic triple-negative breast cancer.
articles.hook: BRCA1 mutations increase B cell activity in triple-negative breast cancer
articles.summary: BRCA1-mutated triple-negative breast cancer has more active B cells than sporadic cases, potentially responding better to immunotherapy.

articles.title: Factors influencing uptake of risk-reducing mastectomy among unaffected Israeli BRCA1/BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers.
articles.hook: Cancer fear and family history drive risk-reducing mastectomy decisions in BRCA carriers
articles.summary: Healthy BRCA gene carriers choosing preventive breast removal are primarily motivated by cancer fear, family history, and support group discussions rather than medical advice.

articles.title: AZD6738 overcomes acquired olaparib resistance in BRCA1 mutation triple-negative breast cancer through down-regulation of BRCA2 and RAD51.
articles.hook: AZD6738 restores olaparib sensitivity in resistant triple-negative breast cancer
articles.summary: AZD6738 combined with olaparib overcomes drug resistance in triple-negative breast cancer by reducing DNA repair proteins.
